name: Château Margaux
blurb: One of the four original 1855 first growths, on the gravel of the Médoc. Cabernet Sauvignon-led reds of perfume and finesse, and a dry white, Pavillon Blanc.

name: Domaine de la Romanée-Conti
blurb: The stone cross marks the Romanée-Conti vineyard itself: under two hectares of Pinot Noir, and the most sought-after wine in Burgundy.

name: Château d’Yquem
blurb: The only Sauternes ranked Premier Cru Supérieur in the 1855 classification. Botrytised Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc that lasts a century.

name: R. López de Heredia
blurb: Founded in 1877 and famous for Viña Tondonia, released only after many years in old oak. The ornate pavilion was made for the 1910 Brussels World Fair.

name: Marqués de Riscal
blurb: One of Rioja’s oldest houses, founded in 1858. Its hotel, wrapped in titanium ribbons, is by Frank Gehry.

name: Tenuta San Guido
blurb: The cypress avenue of Bolgheri leads past the estate that made Sassicaia, the first "Super Tuscan" Cabernet.

name: Dom Pérignon
blurb: Moët & Chandon’s prestige cuvée, named after the Benedictine monk who was cellarmaster at the Abbey of Hautvillers.

name: Scharzhofberg
blurb: A steep slate slope above the Saar and one of Germany’s great Riesling sites, best known through Egon Müller.

name: Penfolds
blurb: Home of Grange, first made experimentally in 1951 and now Australia’s most famous red.

name: Cloudy Bay
blurb: Its first Sauvignon Blanc, in 1985, did more than any other wine to put Marlborough on the map.

name: Catena Zapata
blurb: A winery built as a Mayan-style pyramid, and the pioneer of high-altitude Malbec in the Andes.

name: Opus One
blurb: Founded in 1979 by Robert Mondavi and Baron Philippe de Rothschild of Mouton: Bordeaux blending in Napa.

name: Nyetimber
blurb: A pioneer of English sparkling wine, planting Champagne’s grapes in Sussex from 1988.

name: Vega Sicilia
blurb: Único is released after a decade or more of ageing, and is Spain’s most celebrated red.

name: Mission Estate Winery
blurb: New Zealand’s oldest winery, founded in 1851 by French Marist missionaries at Taradale near Napier. Chardonnay, Syrah and Bordeaux-style reds.

name: Brookfields
blurb: A Hawke’s Bay family winery founded in 1937. Known for Bordeaux-style reds, Syrah and Chardonnay.

name: Church Road
blurb: One of Hawke’s Bay’s oldest names, founded in 1897 at Taradale. Chardonnay, Syrah and Bordeaux-style blends.

name: Trinity Hill
blurb: A Gimblett Gravels pioneer, founded in 1993. Known for Syrah (Homage), Bordeaux-style blends and Chardonnay.

name: Paritua
blurb: A boutique Hawke’s Bay estate making Syrah and Bordeaux-style blends.

name: Torbreck
blurb: Rhône-style Barossa reds, from Shiraz, Grenache and Mataro. Known for The Laird, RunRig and Descendant.

name: Yalumba
blurb: Founded in 1849, Australia’s oldest family-owned winery. Known for Viognier, Shiraz and the Signature cabernet-shiraz.

name: Peter Lehmann
blurb: Founded in 1979 by the “Baron of the Barossa”, who bought fruit from growers when others would not. Generous, good-value Barossa Shiraz.

name: Grant Burge
blurb: A Barossa family estate honouring the 1865 pioneer John Burge. Known for Shiraz, including Meshach.

name: Ministry of Clouds
blurb: A boutique McLaren Vale producer making Grenache, Shiraz and other expressive reds and whites.

name: Yering Station
blurb: Victoria’s oldest vineyard, established in 1838, with a heritage cellar door and a modern restaurant. Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Shiraz Viognier.

name: De Bortoli Yarra Valley
blurb: A family-owned pioneer of premium cool-climate styles, with an Italian restaurant. Noble One Botrytis Semillon, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

name: TarraWarra Estate
blurb: An architectural property with an underground cellar door and a public art museum. Estate Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Barbera.

name: Oakridge Wines
blurb: Precise single-block Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, with a locally sourced fine-dining menu.

name: Dominique Portet Winery
blurb: Founded by a 10th-generation French winemaking family, with a Bordeaux-inspired touch. Rosé, Cabernet Sauvignon and sparkling.

name: Levantine Hill
blurb: A luxury boutique producer of low-yield wines on an upscale estate. Premium Cabernet blends and Syrah.

name: Giant Steps
blurb: A celebrated modern producer focused on single-vineyard Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, expressing specific sub-regional microclimates.

name: Coldstream Hills
blurb: Established by the critic James Halliday in 1985. Elegant, structured Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Merlot.

name: Yarra Yering
blurb: One of the region’s most iconic historic estates. Dry Red No. 1 is a Bordeaux blend and Dry Red No. 2 a Rhône blend, among Australia’s highest-rated reds.

name: Rochford Wines
blurb: A large, lively estate that hosts concerts and festivals as well as alfresco dining. Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Syrah.

name: Medhurst Wines
blurb: A modern boutique winery built into a hillside, making small-batch, low-intervention Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Shiraz.

name: Soumah of Yarra Valley
blurb: Northern Italian varieties beside valley staples, with a trattoria. Savagnin, Nebbiolo and Pinot Noir.

name: Mac Forbes
blurb: A leader of the minimal-intervention, new-wave movement, focused on freshness, acidity and raw terroir. Sub-regional Pinot Noir and experimental whites.

name: Maddens Rise
blurb: A certified organic and biodynamic producer focused on soil health and additive-free fruit. Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Viognier.

name: Seville Estate
blurb: An upper-Yarra pioneer established in 1972, known for long-lived, cool and elegant Shiraz, Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.

name: Innocent Bystander
blurb: A relaxed urban-style cellar door and pizzeria in Healesville. Moscato, Pinot Noir and Gamay.

name: Warramunda Estate
blurb: A family-run boutique vineyard using traditional hand-crafted methods. Viognier, Syrah and Marsanne.

name: Helen & Joey Estate
blurb: A modern, picturesque estate with playful branding and great views. Cabernet, Pinot Noir and sparkling.

name: Coombe Yarra Valley
blurb: The historic former home of Dame Nellie Melba, with century-old gardens. Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling.

name: Punt Road Wines
blurb: Down-to-earth estate-grown wines, a relaxed tasting room and on-site cider. Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and Gamay.
